content: Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid are used for colon cleansing in preparation for a colonoscopy in adults. The preparation requires two doses, which can be administered either as a split-dose regimen or as a day-before regimen. For the product Prepopik, one dose is prepared by dissolving one packet in 5 ounces of cold water using the provided measuring cup. For Clenpiq, one dose is provided as a ready-to-drink 160 mL solution. Patients should be instructed to consume only clear liquids throughout the day before the colonoscopy and on the day of the procedure until two hours prior to the colonoscopy. All fluid intake should be stopped at least two hours before the procedure. Solid foods, dairy products, and beverages that are red or purple in color should be avoided. Alcohol consumption is also prohibited. The safety and efficacy of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid have been established for patients aged 9 years and older. However, these parameters have not been established for children under 9 years of age. This combination can interact with other medications. For example, it decreases the absorption and effectiveness of baloxavir marboxil due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. It is recommended to avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. Similarly, antibiotics can reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora, which is necessary for converting sodium picosulfate into its active form. Examples of antibiotics that may interfere include amikacin, amoxicillin, azithromycin, ceftriaxone, and others. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administering these drugs. Certain medications, such as aspirin, corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone, hydrocortisone), and NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, diclofenac), may increase the risk of fluid and electrolyte imbalances, such as hypokalemia, when used with sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. Close monitoring is recommended in these cases. Additionally, this combination can reduce the absorption of drugs like digoxin, doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, and iron supplements (e.g., ferrous sulfate) due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. To minimize this interaction, these medications should be taken at least two hours before or six hours after the administration of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid.
